newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania starts $24 million harbour renovation.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania starts $24 million harbour renovation.

text.p: Work has started on a $24 million project to widen the harbour entrance at Dar es Salaam port as part of a modernisation programme to boost traffic, state-run Tanzanian Harbours Authority (THA) said on Friday.
In a statement sent to Reuters, the THA said dredging will take up to 40 weeks in which an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of harbour floor will be excavated.

"Entrance channel conditions and characteristics at the port of Dar es Salaam do not allow easy entry of big internal trade ships. As such the port is disadvantaged to compete with other big ports in the region," the statement said.
Nightime navigation is currently banned for ships arriving or leaving the port -- causing delays of up to 22 hours and additional expense for the government.
The harbour entrance channel will be widened, deepened and straightened, THA said. It said this would enable the entrance of larger ships and extend the working hours of the port.
The depth of the entrance channel will be increased from 7.4 metres (24.42 ft) to 10 metres (33 ft) while underwater obstacles and wrecks will be removed.

Modernisation of Dar es Salaam port is being spurred by increasing competition among ports along the African east coast especially, Kenya's Indian Ocean terminal at Mombasa, Mozambique's Maputo and East London in South Africa.
One side effect of the modernisation programme will be the closure and relocation of Dar es Salaam's colourful old fish market, according to local traders.
